title: Clock rate and acceleration from rest of a body with position-dependent factors

key_results.statement: Weak records, exact on the chain $\lvert x\rvert\le L$ for every member, start and $\lambda$: body expectations differ from those of $e^{-iC_{\rm eff}\lambda}\phi$ by at most $2\kappa^2\sigma_X^2L^2\lambda^2\lVert O\rVert$.
Velocity operator of the class: $\mathrm d\bar x_{\rm lab}/\mathrm d\lambda=\langle\hat v\rangle$ with $\hat v=-\frac{\tau}{2}\sum_x\zeta_x(R_x+R_x^\dagger)\otimes\sigma_1$, exact for every $\kappa$.

Acceleration operator: $\hat a=\frac{\tau^2}{2}\sum_x(\zeta_x^2-\zeta_{x-1}^2)P_x+\frac{\tau}{2}\sum_x\zeta_x[(R_x+R_x^\dagger)\sigma_2(\mathsf M_x+\mathsf M_{x+1})+(V_{x+1}-V_x)(-iR_x+iR_x^\dagger)\sigma_1]$, with end terms on the open chain.

Exact second derivative for every $\kappa$: $\mathrm d^2\bar x_{\rm lab}/\mathrm d\lambda^2=\langle\hat a\otimes 1+\kappa A_\zeta\otimes(X-\langle X\rangle)\rangle$; the second term is $0$ at $\lambda=0$ and at most $2\kappa^2\sigma_X^2\tau\zeta_{\max}L\lambda$ later.
For $S_k$ and $S'_k$, exactly: $\mathrm d\bar x_{\rm lab}/\mathrm d\lambda(0)=0$ and $\mathrm d^2\bar x_{\rm lab}/\mathrm d\lambda^2(0)=\frac{\tau^2}{2}\sum_x(\zeta_x^2-\zeta_{x-1}^2)\phi_X(x)^2$.

First-order acceleration of the start $S_k$ at finite $W$ on the infinite chain: $a^{(1)}_W(\lambda)=\langle\alpha(p,\lambda)\rangle_W$ with $\alpha$ smooth, even in $p$ and independent of $x_0$; the zeroth order vanishes.

Wide-start limit at fixed $\lambda$: $a^{(1)}_\infty(\lambda)=\tau^2g_\zeta\cos(2M_k\lambda)+\frac{2\tau^2}{M_k}(\mathcal F-G_k)\sin^2(M_k\lambda)-2\tau^2G_k\lambda\sin(2M_k\lambda)$, $G_k=mg_m+d_kg_\eta$.

Finite width: $\lvert a^{(1)}_W-a^{(1)}_\infty\rvert\le\frac{\pi^2}{8}\delta_W^2\sup_p\lvert\partial_p^2\alpha\rvert$ (exact) with $\sup_p\lvert\partial_p^2\alpha\rvert\le c\,\tau b_1(1+M_k\lambda)(1+\tau\lambda)^3$ (order estimate) and $\delta_W^2=O(W^{-2})$.

Wide-start first-order velocity: $v^{(1)}_\infty=\frac{\tau^2}{M_k}(\mathcal F-G_k)\lambda+\frac{\tau^2G_k}{M_k}\lambda\cos(2M_k\lambda)+\frac{\tau^2}{2M_k^2}(M_kg_\zeta-\mathcal F)\sin(2M_k\lambda)$.

Window average with the wide start first: $\overline{a^{(1)}_\infty}=\frac{\tau^2}{M_k}[(\mathcal F-G_k)+G_k\varsigma+(M_kg_\zeta-\mathcal F)\rho]$; $\varsigma=\cos(2M_kT)+O(\lambda_1/\Lambda)$ does not decay, so the coefficients of $g_m$, $g_\eta$ have no long-window limit.

Additional result: secular acceleration $a_{\rm sec}:=\frac{\tau^2}{M_k}(\mathcal F-G_k)$, the coefficient of $\frac12\lambda^2$ in the wide-start first-order displacement; it is not the window average of item 2(b).

Exact second-order remainder on any chain (open ends included) within $\ell$ of the expansion point, if $b_1\ell\le\tau+M_k$: $\lvert a-a^{(0)}_\ell-a^{(1)}_\ell\rvert\le16\,\tau(\tau+M_k)[b_1\ell(\lambda+(\tau+M_k)^{-1})]^2$ for all $\lambda\ge0$.

Well-defined form with the wide start first: $\overline{a^{(1)}_\infty}=\frac{8t^2}{\Delta_k}[-\delta E^+_k+\frac12\delta\Delta_k\varsigma+(\frac{\Delta_k}{2}\frac{\delta t}{t}+\frac12(\delta E^+_k+\delta E^-_k))\rho]$, and $a_{\rm sec}=\lim_{W\to\infty}\bar a_W=-\frac{8t^2}{\Delta_k}\delta E^+_k$.

Other branch $S'_k$, wide start: $a'^{(1)}_\infty$ is (3.11) with $\mathcal F\to-\mathcal F$ in the $\sin^2$ term, and $a'_{\rm sec}=-\frac{\tau^2}{M_k}(\mathcal F+G_k)=+\frac{8t^2}{\Delta_k}\delta E^-_k$ (additional result).
Additional result, limits $W\to\infty$ of $\bar a_W$ for the variants: (a) $-g\tau^2$; (b1) $-g\tau^2m/(m+d_k)$; (b2) $-g\tau^2d_k/(m+d_k)$; (c) $-g\tau^2$; (d) $\tau^2\mathcal F/(m+d_k)$.

Uniform profiles: $q(a;\lambda)=P_N(a;\Gamma_\ast(p_0)\eta_\ast\lambda/\lambda_0)+\mathcal R_\ast$ with $\Gamma_\ast=\bar\mu_\ast/\sqrt{\bar\mu_\ast^2+\tau^2\zeta_\ast^2\sin^2p_0}$, $\bar\mu_\ast=m_\ast+\eta_\ast\bar d$.
Tick for uniform profiles: $\lambda_\ast(p_0)=\lambda_0/(\eta_\ast\Gamma_\ast(p_0))$ and $\lambda_\ast(0)=\lambda_0/\eta_\ast$, independent of $m_\ast$, $\zeta_\ast$, $V_\ast$.

Linear profiles, start $S_{\rm clock}(x_0)$, every real $w$, exact: $\lvert q(a;\lambda)-P_N(a;\eta_{x_0}\lambda/\lambda_0)\rvert\le\delta_W^2\frac{\tau^{0\,2}}{m_{x_0}^2}(2+\frac{\pi\eta_{x_0}\lambda}{\lambda_0})+2b_{\rm cl}\lambda(W+\frac12+\frac12\tau^0\lambda)+4e^{\theta_0}\theta_0^r/r!+2\kappa^2\sigma_X^2L^2\lambda^2$; the first term is the finite-width term and does not vanish in the zeroth-gradient limit.

Rate at $x_0$ := wide-start limit of the finite-width rate: $\lim_{W\to\infty}r_W=\eta_{x_0}/\lambda_0=\frac{N}{2\pi}(E^+_{x_0,k+1}-E^+_{x_0,k})$, tick $\lambda_0/\eta_{x_0}$; at finite $W$ the rate is $\frac{\eta_{x_0}}{\lambda_0}(1-\varsigma_W)$ with $\lvert r_W-\eta_{x_0}/\lambda_0\rvert\le\frac{\eta_{x_0}}{\lambda_0}\delta_W^2\tau^{0\,2}/m_{x_0}^2$.

Ratio of rates at two places, compared at equal $\lambda$ (A8), same $w$ and $W$: $\frac{\eta_{x_1}}{\eta_{x_2}}\cdot\frac{1-\varsigma_W(x_1)}{1-\varsigma_W(x_2)}$; wide start: $(1+gx_1)/(1+gx_2)$ in (a), (b2), (c) and $1$ in (b1), (d); the finite-width factor is exactly $1$ in (c), (d), differs from $1$ in (a), (b1), and deviates from $1$ by at most $\delta_W^2\lvert\varkappa_1^2-\varkappa_2^2\rvert(1+\varkappa_2^2)$.

For the acceleration of item 2(a) and its window average at finite $W$ or with the wide start first, no variant is the same for all $k$ and $m$; in the iterated limit $\Lambda\to\infty$ then $W\to\infty$, with the clock rate in the wide-start approximation, only (a) and (c) have both a window average independent of $k$, $m$ ($-g\tau^2$) and a place-dependent clock rate; at finite $W$ (b1) also has a place-dependent rate at relative order $\delta_W^2\tau^2/m^2$.

Exact structure of the first-order velocity density: $\nu(p,\lambda)=a_{\rm sec}(p)\lambda+\nu_0(p)+\operatorname{Re}\sum_{j\le2}\lambda^jA_j(p)e^{2i\omega_k\lambda}$ with $a_{\rm sec}(p)=\frac{g_\zeta\tau^4\sin^2p-G_k\tau^2M_k\cos2p}{\omega_k^2}+\mathcal F\frac{\tau^2M_k(M_k^2\cos2p-\tau^2\sin^4p)}{\omega_k^4}$ and $A_2=-i\mathcal FM_k\omega_k'^{\,2}/\omega_k$.

At every finite $W$ the long-window limit of the window average exists: $\bar a_W=\langle a_{\rm sec}(p)\rangle_W=g_\zeta\tau^4s_W-\frac{\tau^2G_k}{M_k}[1-(2M_k^2+\tau^2)s_W]+\frac{\tau^2\mathcal F}{M_k}f_W$, with $0<s_W\le\delta_W^2/M_k^2$ and $0\le1-f_W\le2(M_k^2+\tau^2)s_W$; the oscillating remainder is $O(\lambda^{1/2})$ and grows as $\lambda^{1/2}$ for $G_k\neq0$ and for $\mathcal F\neq0$.

$\lvert\bar a_W-a_{\rm sec}\rvert\le2\delta_W^2\frac{\tau^2}{M_k}(1+\frac{\tau^2}{M_k^2})b_1$ (exact), so $\lim_{W\to\infty}\lim_{\Lambda\to\infty}\overline{a^{(1)}_W}=a_{\rm sec}$, while $\lim_{\Lambda\to\infty}\lim_{W\to\infty}$ does not exist for $G_k\neq0$: the limits do not commute.

Well-defined form at finite $W$: $\bar a_W=16t^3\delta t\,s_W-\frac{4t^2}{\Delta_k}\delta\Delta_k[1-(\frac12\Delta_k^2+4t^2)s_W]-\frac{4t^2}{\Delta_k}(\delta E^+_k+\delta E^-_k)f_W$, in gaps, hopping norms and neighbour differences of on-site eigenvalues.
Other branch $S'_k$ at finite $W$, long window: $\bar a'_W=g_\zeta\tau^4s_W-\frac{\tau^2G_k}{M_k}[1-(2M_k^2+\tau^2)s_W]-\frac{\tau^2\mathcal F}{M_k}f_W$; only the $\mathcal F$ term changes sign.

Variants, $\bar a_W$ for $S_k$: (a) $-g\tau^2(1-u_W)$; (b1) $-g\tau^2\frac{m}{M_k}(1-u_W)$; (b2) $-g\tau^2\frac{d_k}{M_k}(1-u_W)$; (c) $-g\tau^2(1-u^{\rm c}_W)$; (d) $\frac{\tau^2\mathcal F}{M_k}f_W$, with $u_W=(2M_k^2+\tau^2)s_W$, $u^{\rm c}_W=2(M_k^2+\tau^2)s_W$.

Absolute error of the double average: $\lvert2[\bar x^{(1)}_{\rm lab}(\Lambda)-\bar x_{\rm lab}(0)]/\Lambda^2-a_{\rm sec}\rvert\le\frac{\tau^2\lvert G_k\rvert}{M_k^2\Lambda}+\frac{\tau^2\lvert M_kg_\zeta-\mathcal F-G_k\rvert}{M_k^3\Lambda^2}$.

Even $w$ and a chain symmetric about $x_0$: $q$ is even in the gradients jointly (exact), and $\lvert q-q_{\rm loc}\rvert\le c[b_{\rm cl}\lambda(W+1+\tau_{\max}\lambda)]^2$ (order estimate); for every real $w$ the same bound holds for $q-q_{\rm loc}-\delta^{(1)}q$.

Start $S_{\rm clock}(x_0)$ at zeroth order in the gradients and finite $W$, exact on the infinite chain: $q_{\rm loc}(a;\lambda)=\langle Q(a;p,\lambda)\rangle_W$ with $Q=\lVert\frac1N\sum_ke^{2\pi ika/N}\chi_{k,\lambda}(p)\rVert^2$, $\chi_{k,\lambda}=e^{-i\omega_k\lambda}P^{(k)}_+\lvert1\rangle+e^{i\omega_k\lambda}P^{(k)}_-\lvert1\rangle$.

First order in the level spacing at finite $W$: $q_{\rm loc}=\langle\frac{1+\Gamma}{2}P_N(a;\Gamma\eta_{x_0}\lambda/\lambda_0)+\frac{1-\Gamma}{2}P_N(a;-\Gamma\eta_{x_0}\lambda/\lambda_0)\rangle_W+\mathcal R_W$ with $\Gamma(p)=\bar\mu/\sqrt{\bar\mu^2+\tau^{0\,2}\sin^2p}$ and, exactly, $\lvert\mathcal R_W\rvert\le\delta_W^2\frac{\tau^{0\,2}}{m_{x_0}^2}\upsilon[4+\upsilon+\pi\upsilon\eta_{x_0}\lambda/\lambda_0]$, $\upsilon=\pi\eta_{x_0}/(\lambda_0m_{x_0})$.

Advance and rate at finite $W$: $\vartheta_W=(1-\varsigma_W)\eta_{x_0}\lambda/\lambda_0$ (mean advance of the mixture), $r_W=\frac{\eta_{x_0}}{\lambda_0}(1-\varsigma_W)$ constant in $\lambda$, $\varsigma_W=\langle\tau^{0\,2}\sin^2p/(\bar\mu^2+\tau^{0\,2}\sin^2p)\rangle_W$ with $0<\varsigma_W\le\delta_W^2\tau^{0\,2}/\bar\mu^2$; it depends on $m$ and $\tau$.

Exact first-order term in the gradients for every real $w$ on the infinite chain: $\delta^{(1)}q=\langle\xi_y(p)\partial_yQ(a;p,\lambda)\rangle_W$, $\lvert\delta^{(1)}q\rvert\le2b_{\rm cl}\lambda W$, $\partial_yQ(a;0,\lambda)=g_\eta\frac{\lambda}{\lambda_0}\partial_\vartheta P_N$; it is a position term, the beginning motion and the plain gradient contribute nothing at first order.

open_issues: The amplitudes ν_0, A_0, A_1 of (3.26) are not given in closed form for p ≠ 0 and the constant c_W is not determined; the late-time forms of Step 5.2 are leading stationary-phase terms, the statements for λ ≪ λ_W assume W ≥ τ/M_k, and the coefficient of the decaying bond-gradient oscillation is not computed.

(3.27) and (3.14) are statements about the first Taylor coefficient; the range (3.16) is a sufficient condition, the sharp range is not determined, and the growing oscillation beyond first order is not derived here.
For variant (a) the dependence of the finite-W average on M_k is shown to be present for wide starts only (order estimate); for variant (c) it is exact for every start.

Clock at finite W: the advance is defined as the mean of the mixture (3.35), fixed by the description and not by q alone, and from the first-order form only; the dependence of the rate and of the ratio (3.24) on N, λ_0 and the level structure beyond the common level spacing is of the order of the remainder and is not determined (it needs second order in the level spacing), including the finite-width factor of variant (b2).

Item 3(b), first nonzero orders: not determined for the width when g_η = 0 and for the second-order motion coefficients of g_m, g_ζ and g_η; proven there are the vanishing of the first-order motion term and the upper bounds.
For unbounded bond profiles the limit of a long chain is not shown.
The rates at two places are compared across two runs through A8; a comparison inside one description is not treated.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions (accelerations and a_sec(p): 1/λ²; velocities, the density ν of (3.26), ν_0, A_0: 1/λ; A_1: 1/λ²; A_2: 1/λ³; rates: 1/λ; clock distributions, bounds, ς_W, υ: none) and the case of zero gradients: Model D operators of (6.12), vanishing (3.11), (3.27), (3.37), q = q_loc, ratio 1 at every W.

Variant (d) against (6.12), (6.13), (6.24), (6.15), (6.20); second route to A_2 through the exact shift of the plane-wave label in (9.1): the only λ² term is F (M_k/ω_k) ω_k'² λ² sin(2 ω_k λ), the secular term is F ω_k'' M_k/ω_k, and p = 0 gives the F part of (3.13); no first-order clock term, as ϑ_1 of (9.12) is even in F at p_0 = 0.

Independent routes for the clock results: Duhamel in the level gives Γ² λ + τ² sin²p sin(2ωλ)/(2ω³), whose secular part is the mean advance of (3.36) and whose oscillating part is the first-order term of the remainder; the upper-branch part of (3.35) is the form (3.20); the exact proportionality of the local contract in variant (c) gives the ratio at every W; τ → 0 gives ς_W → 0 and the exact mixture over places; the branch function reproduces the coefficients of a_sec(p).

response_to_verification.where: Step 5, parts 5.1 and 5.2: explicit A_2 in (3.26) and the late-time estimate for every gradient
